before.title: Battery Drain / No-Start from Telematics, Infotainment, or Control Module Sleep Issues
before.description: Owners of the redesigned QX60 have reported dead batteries, repeated jump-starts, and no-start conditions after the vehicle sits overnight or for a few days. Complaints and forum reports point to parasitic draw from modules that do not go to sleep properly, including telematics and infotainment-related systems, rather than a simple worn battery in many low-mileage cases. The problem is especially frustrating because battery replacement alone may not permanently fix it.
before.solution: Perform a proper parasitic draw test after all modules should be asleep, then isolate the circuit causing excess current draw. Check for TSB/software updates for telematics/AV modules, test battery health, and inspect charging system output; some vehicles need module reprogramming, while others require battery replacement after repeated deep discharge damage. Document draw readings before replacing parts.
symptoms: Dead battery after sitting overnight or a few days
No crank or clicking on startup

citations.title: NHTSA complaints for 2022-2025 Infiniti QX60 battery drain / no-start

communityRecommendations.content: Ask for a parasitic draw test printout instead of accepting a battery swap as the only diagnosis.
If the vehicle sits often, a smart maintainer can prevent deep discharge while the root cause is being diagnosed.

before.title: CVT Transmission Failure
before.description: The Jatco CVT in the QX60 is prone to premature failure, particularly in the 2013-2017 models. The transmission overheats during towing or sustained highway driving, leading to shuddering, slipping, and eventual complete failure.
before.solution: Replace CVT fluid every 30,000 miles instead of the recommended 60,000. Add an auxiliary transmission cooler for towing. Nissan extended the CVT warranty to 84 months/84,000 miles on affected models.

before.title: Forward Collision Warning / Automatic Emergency Braking False Activation or Unexpected Braking
before.description: Owners have reported unexpected forward collision warnings and abrupt braking events with no obvious obstacle ahead, especially in traffic, on curves, or near roadside objects. These complaints are tied to the QX60's ADAS sensor/camera interpretation rather than a conventional brake hardware fault. Sudden braking can create a rear-impact hazard and is one of the more serious owner-reported safety concerns on the current generation.
before.solution: Scan the ADAS system for stored faults and verify radar/camera alignment, windshield condition, and front emblem/radar cleanliness. Infiniti service procedures typically involve checking for software updates, recalibrating the forward camera/radar, and replacing a faulty sensor only after alignment and aiming are confirmed. Owners should document the exact conditions when the event occurs to help reproduce the issue.
symptoms: Forward collision warning with no vehicle ahead
Dash warning messages for FEB/AEB or front sensor

citations.title: NHTSA complaints for 2022-2025 Infiniti QX60 involving false braking / FCW-AEB behavior

communityRecommendations.content: Keep the front emblem/radar area and windshield camera area clean; contamination can worsen false alerts.
After windshield replacement or front-end work, insist on proper ADAS calibration rather than assuming the system will self-learn.

before.title: Panoramic Moonroof Exploding or Cracking Spontaneously
before.description: A number of current-generation QX60 owners have reported the panoramic glass roof suddenly cracking or shattering with a loud bang while driving, often without any clear impact evidence. Complaints commonly describe the inner shade catching falling glass and the damage appearing to originate upward, consistent with tempered glass breakage rather than a direct rock strike. While not universal, the reports are repeated enough to be a known owner concern on the redesigned model.
before.solution: Inspect the glass carefully for impact point evidence and document the break pattern before replacement. Repair requires replacing the affected moonroof glass panel and checking frame alignment, seal fitment, and drain condition; if there is no impact evidence, owners should pursue warranty/goodwill review and file a safety complaint. Avoid driving with exposed broken glass until the panel is secured or replaced.
symptoms: Loud popping or gunshot-like noise from roof

citations.title: NHTSA complaints for 2022-2024 Infiniti QX60 panoramic sunroof shattering

communityRecommendations.content: Take photos of the glass pattern before cleanup; owners report this helps when disputing a denied warranty claim.
Use OEM glass and have the shop verify drain routing and frame alignment during replacement.

before.title: Power Steering Pump Whine
before.description: The hydraulic power steering pump develops a pronounced whining noise, especially during cold starts and low-speed turning. Air intrusion into the power steering fluid or a failing pump bearing causes the noise.
before.solution: Flush the power steering system and refill with Nissan PSF. Bleed air from the system by turning the wheel lock-to-lock several times with the engine running. Replace the pump if the noise persists after fluid service.

before.title: Rearview Camera Image Blank, Distorted, or Intermittent Due to Infotainment/Display Software
before.description: Multiple owners of the redesigned 2022+ QX60 reported the backup camera showing a black screen, frozen image, delayed image, or distorted view when shifting into reverse. This is safety-significant because the rearview image may not display as required, and Infiniti/Nissan issued a recall covering certain vehicles for software that can cause the center information display not to show the rearview camera image. Owner complaints describe intermittent failures that may temporarily clear after a restart but recur unpredictably.
before.solution: Confirm the concern by checking for intermittent camera loss, delayed display, or frozen image when selecting reverse. Inspect for open recalls and apply the latest AV/control unit software update per Infiniti/Nissan service procedure; if the issue persists, diagnose the display control unit, camera harness, and rear camera module for faults or poor connections. Vehicles still under recall/warranty should have the software remedy performed first.
symptoms: Black screen when shifting into reverse
Rear camera image delayed or frozen
Distorted or blank center display image
Issue may clear after key cycle and return later

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 24V-321 / Nissan-Infiniti rearview camera display software issue

communityRecommendations.content: Check VIN for open rearview camera/display recalls before paying for diagnosis; many owners resolved it with the software campaign.
If the recall update does not fix it, ask the dealer to inspect the rear camera connector and hatch harness for intermittent connection issues.

before.title: Transmission Judder at Low Speed
before.description: The QX60 CVT exhibits a pronounced judder during low-speed maneuvers such as parking lot driving and stop-and-go traffic. The torque converter and CVT belt interaction produces an uncomfortable vibration through the drivetrain.
before.solution: Have the dealer perform the CVT judder reprogram (TSB NTB15-024). A CVT fluid change with NS-3 fluid can also improve the condition. Drive the vehicle for 30 minutes after the fluid change to allow the TCM to relearn.
